English translation from the Modern Amharic of the EOTC Bible (nehemiah-osc.org) by Claude (Anthropic) with collaborator, May 2026. Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication (archive.org/details/three-books-of-meqabyan-cc0-translation). Apparatus integrates Josef Horovitz, 'Das äthiopische Maccabäerbuch,' Zeitschrift für Assyriologie XIX (1905), pp. 194-233 — PD primary scholarly study. 64-citation third-pass audit verdict matrix; 57 verified, 4 errors corrected, 3 interpretive readings flagged, 7 newly discovered parallels added. Dating widened to Aksumite-to-Solomonic Ethiopian Christian range (4th-14th c. CE); precise composition date undetermined in current scholarship per Horovitz 1905 non-commitment. Three books: 1 Mq 36 chapters (Maqabis-of-Benjamin martyrology vs Ṣiruṣaydan); 2 Mq 21 chapters (Maqabis-of-Moab conversion + sons' martyrdom + Ṣiruṣaydan's death); 3 Mq 10 chapters (homiletic + angelological dialogue + Satan-refused-Adam tradition + resurrection-doctrine).

OPENS Ch 22 — HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR: covenant-renewal-homiletic + rebuke-of-king theme. The chapter likely develops the prophetic-rebuke-of-the-king theme established earlier in the trilogy (cf. 2 Mq 2:1 prophet Re'ay confronts Maqabis-of-Moab γ.4.8 seed; 1 Mq 7:1 sons' direct-address-to-king γ.4.8.B entry). Direct biblical parallels for the rebuke-of-king pattern: NATHAN-TO-DAVID 2 SAMUEL 12 (Nathan's 'thou art the man' parable-rebuke); ELIJAH-TO-AHAB 1 KINGS 21:17-29 (after Naboth's-vineyard); ELIJAH-TO-AHAZIAH 2 KINGS 1:1-17; AMOS-TO-AMAZIAH-AT-BETHEL Amos 7:10-17; ISAIAH-TO-AHAZ Isaiah 7:1-17; JEREMIAH-TO-JEHOIAKIM Jeremiah 36:29-30; JOHN-THE-BAPTIST-TO-HEROD-ANTIPAS Mark 6:17-29 par. The Meqabyan chapter likely extends the prophetic-rebuke-of-king pattern to a STRUCTURAL-CULMINATION before the chapter's covenant-renewal theme (mirroring 2 Mq Ch 3's pit-immersion-conversion + Ch 4 idols-and-sorcerers-purge γ.4.8.C entries).

HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR — likely development of DAVIDIC-COVENANT extension to Tewahedo-monarchy. The Tewahedo-monarchic-tradition (Solomonic dynasty per Kǝbrä Nägäśt) reads Davidic-covenant-succession-promises (2 SAMUEL 7:8-17 + PSALM 89:3-4 + PSALM 132:11-12) as fulfilled in the Tewahedo-emperors' Solomonic descent. The Davidic-covenant theme parallels: 2 SAMUEL 7:8-17 (the foundational-Davidic covenant); 1 CHRONICLES 17:7-15 (the parallel-formulation); PSALM 89:3-4 + 89:28-37 (the Davidic-eternal-covenant); ISAIAH 11:1-10 (the rod-from-the-stem-of-Jesse messianic-Davidic); JEREMIAH 23:5-6 + 33:14-22 (the Davidic-righteous-Branch); ZECHARIAH 12:8-10 (the day-of-the-LORD Davidic-context); LUKE 1:32-33 (Christ as Davidic-throne-heir); ROMANS 1:3 (Christ-of-the-seed-of-David-according-to-the-flesh); 2 TIMOTHY 2:8 (remember Jesus Christ of the seed of David). Tewahedo Kǝbrä Nägäśt (Book of the Glory of the Kings, 13th c.) preserves the Tewahedo-Solomonic-Davidic dynastic-succession-tradition tracing Menelik I → Solomon → Tewahedo-monarchy.

HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR — likely development of KING-AS-SERVANT-OF-GOD theme. The royal-servanthood theme parallels: 1 KINGS 8:14-53 (Solomon's-temple-dedication prayer); 1 CHRONICLES 29:10-19 (David's-dedication prayer); ISAIAH 42:1-9 + 49:1-7 + 50:4-11 + 52:13-53:12 (the Suffering-Servant songs — read Christologically); PHILIPPIANS 2:5-11 (Christ-as-servant kenosis — paired with 3 Mq 7:7 γ.4.8.D entry on humility); 1 PETER 2:21-25 (Christ-our-example-of-suffering-servant). Tewahedo Christological tradition preserves the king-as-servant-of-God paradigm in the Tewahedo-imperial-coronation-ritual (the emperor explicitly-confessed-as-servant-of-the-Holy-Trinity at coronation per the 1956 Constitutional documents codified from the older Fetha Nagast tradition). The Meqabyan chapter likely synthesizes the rebuke-of-evil-king (vv. 1-13) with the model-of-righteous-king-as-servant (vv. 14-end).
